title: HTTP timeout does not cover smoke response-body reads
test: tests/smokePackaged.test.js (new): 'the JSON read gives up at the timeout when the server sends headers and never ends the body', 'the text read gives up at the timeout when the server sends headers and never ends the body', 'a call that does not read the body returns at the headers and drops a body that never ends', 'no stage reads a response body outside the bounded fetchWithTimeout helper', plus 'requiring smoke-packaged.js exports its helpers and does not run the smoke' and guards for the helper's results, a non-JSON body, an unknown read mode, a server that never sends headers, an unreachable server and isReadyBody
proof: Holds. fetchWithTimeout cleared its abort timer as soon as fetch() resolved (response headers), and every stage then called response.json() or response.text() outside any timeout, so a server that sends headers and never ends the body left waitReady, the static-shell, handshake, package-info and media-worker stages (and the readiness poll inside the worker replacement loop) pending forever and the cleanup after the stages never ran. The file also ran main() on require, so it could not be loaded by a test. Before the fix: the new test file failed 11 of 11 on the unchanged code (the helpers were not exported: 'smoke.fetchWithTimeout is not a function'; requiring the file ran main(), which printed 'Packaged executable not found' and set exit code 1). Because that failure is about the missing export and not about the stall, the stall itself was shown on the unchanged code with a script that extracts the real fetchWithTimeout from the file and reads the body the way the call sites did, against a local server that sends headers plus '{"status":' and never ends: with a 300 ms timeout the read was still pending when the check gave up at 5x the timeout (1525 ms). Fix: fetchWithTimeout(url, options, timeoutMs, read) takes read = 'json' | 'text' | 'none' (default 'none'; anything else throws a TypeError before the request), awaits response.json() / response.text() (or response.body?.cancel() for 'none') inside the try block, before clearTimeout, and returns { status, ok, body }. All call sites use it (waitReady, checkStaticShell, checkSocketHandshake, checkPackageInfo, checkMediaWorkerReplacement incl. its polling loop, checkGracefulShutdown's shutdown POST and /healthz probe, cleanup's shutdown POST); no stage touches a Response any more, the timeout values, stage order, log lines and failure messages are unchanged. main().catch(...) runs only under require.main === module and the helpers and stages are exported. With the fix: the JSON and text reads reject with AbortError after about 300 ms for a headers-only stall and a partial-body stall (asserted below 300 ms + 2 s), the 'none' read returns at the headers with body null, and driving the real stage functions against a fake packaged server on port 31847 (not committed) shows each stage rejecting at its own timeout (waitReady 2.5 s for one attempt, the others 5 s) with a stalled body and all passing against a healthy one.
